_meta.indication: Treatment of adults with confirmed Fabry disease

pivotal_trials.phase: Open-label, single-arm, dose-ranging trial (primary support for efficacy)
pivotal_trials.design: Single-arm, open-label, dose-ranging study; renal PTC biopsy for Gb3 inclusions at baseline and 6 months
pivotal_trials.population: Adult ERT-naïve Fabry disease patients (or off ERT for at least 26 weeks with negative anti-drug antibody)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Reduction from baseline in renal Gb3 inclusions in kidney peritubular capillaries (BLISS score) at 6 months
pivotal_trials.n: 18 enrolled; 14 patients had evaluable renal biopsies at baseline and Month 6 for the main efficacy analysis
pivotal_trials.result: Median absolute reduction in renal Gb3 BLISS score -2.5 (95% CI: -5.3, -0.7; p = 0.001), median percent reduction -78%; 11/14 (79%) patients had a nominally significant reduction (p<0.001)

pivotal_trials.phase: Phase 3 randomized, double-blind, active-controlled trial (used as confirmatory evidence)
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized 2:1, active-controlled, parallel-group; ELFABRIO vs agalsidase beta, 1 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks for up to 24 months
pivotal_trials.population: ERT-experienced adults with Fabry disease with impaired renal function, previously treated with agalsidase beta
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Annualized rate of change of eGFR (eGFR slope)
pivotal_trials.result: Mean eGFR slopes -2.4 (PRX102) vs -2.3 (agalsidase beta) mL/min/1.73 m2/year; treatment difference -0.1 (95% CI: -2.2, 2.1), demonstrating comparable eGFR slope between arms

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥15%): infusion-associated reactions (32%), nasopharyngitis (21%) and headache (21%), diarrhea (19%), fatigue (17%) and nausea (17%), back pain, pain in extremity and sinusitis (each 15%). Serious risks include hypersensitivity reactions/anaphylaxis and IARs (29% experienced one or more IARs); a case of membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis was reported.
target_moa: PEGylated, covalently cross-linked recombinant human alpha-galactosidase A enzyme (produced in plant cells) that replaces the deficient lysosomal enzyme in Fabry disease, reducing accumulation of the substrate globotriaosylceramide (Gb3)
modality: Enzyme (PEGylated recombinant human alpha-galactosidase A enzyme replacement therapy)

boxed_warning.content: Hypersensitivity reactions including anaphylaxis: patients treated with ELFABRIO have experienced hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis; discontinue immediately and initiate treatment if severe reaction occurs.

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an FDA advisory committee because this biologic is not the first in its class

The applicant had a Fast Track Designation (January 29, 2018). Following resubmission (received November 9, 2022) with Study F20 as confirmatory evidence, the product received traditional (full) approval May 9, 2023 as a Standard review; no accelerated approval, orphan, breakthrough, or priority-review designation applied.

requirement.text: 3972-1: Clinical trial to evaluate safety, efficacy, PK, and PD of pegunigalsidase alfa-ixwj in pediatric patients aged 2 to <18 years with confirmed Fabry disease (deferred pediatric study)

citations.quote: 3972-1 Clinical trial to evaluate the safety, efficacy, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamic effects of pegunigalsidase alfa-ixwj in pediatric patients aged 2 to <18 years with confirmed Fabry disease. The trial will evaluate patients over at least 1 year from the time of enrollment and will include assessments of immunogenicity and correlative analyses between antibody formation (and titers if appropriate) and safety, efficacy, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics in treated patients.
